title: Lesson 4: The Bible
description: The Bible is not just a book to read. It is how the God who made you speaks to you. This lesson gives you the Three Discovery Questions, a simple tool used by disciples around the world, so you can read any passage, hear from God, and respond.

blocks.text: In the last lesson, you learned to pray using the pattern Jesus gave in the Lord's Prayer. Prayer is how you talk to God. Now you will learn a simple way to listen to Him through the Bible: Read, discover, respond.

blocks.title: Questions in the Night
blocks.text:
Nicodemus came to Jesus at night. He was a respected religious teacher who knew the Scriptures, yet Jesus said something he did not understand: he must be born again.

Nicodemus asked how an old man could be born a second time. Jesus spoke of new life through the Spirit and of God's love in giving His Son, so that those who believe in Him have eternal life (John 3:1-17).

Nicodemus had more to learn, and Jesus gave him words worth listening to. You can begin there too, with your Bible open and room for questions.
God Speaks Through His Word

The Bible is God's Word, given so that you can know Him, trust Him, and follow Him. Its books tell the story of God creating a good world, people turning from Him, and His rescue through Jesus. When you open it, you are learning who God is and what He has done for you.
All Scripture is breathed out by God and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for training in righteousness, that the man of God may be complete, equipped for every good work.

God has spoken because He wants to be known. Reading Scripture is a way to receive His truth and care, not a task you complete to earn His love. A few verses read with attention give you something to carry into your day. As you return to His Word, you learn to recognize what is true and respond with trust.
4.1 - How has reading the Gospel of John affected you so far?
Read, Discover, Respond

Choose a short passage and read it slowly, more than once if you need to. Notice who is speaking and what is happening. Then ask three questions to help you pay attention to God, to people, and to the response His Word calls for.

blocks.title: The Three Discovery Questions
content: 1. What does this passage tell me about God? Look for what God says and does. What does the passage show about His character, His promises, or His care for people?
2. What does this passage tell me about people? Notice what people say, believe, and do. What does the passage show about their need, their choices, or their response to God?

3. What is this passage calling me to do or believe? Look for a truth to trust, a command to follow, a sin to turn from, or a promise to hold on to. Let your response grow from what the passage actually says.

blocks.text: These questions give you a place to begin. If something is unclear, read the verses around it and ask a trusted Christian to help. You do not have to force an answer or find a hidden message. Stay with what the passage says, and let a clear truth guide your response.
Try It: Nicodemus Meets Jesus

Return to Nicodemus's conversation with Jesus. Read these verses slowly, then answer the three questions. The quotation includes the opening of their conversation and the promise in verses 16-17. You can read the whole conversation in John 3:1-21.

<sup>1</sup>Now there was a man of the Pharisees named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews. <sup>2</sup>This man came to Jesus by night and said to him, "Rabbi, we know that you are a teacher come from God, for no one can do these signs that you do unless God is with him." <sup>3</sup>Jesus answered him, "Truly, truly, I say to you, unless one is born again he cannot see the kingdom of God." <sup>4</sup>Nicodemus said to him, "How can a man be born when he is old? Can he enter a second time into his mother's womb and be born?" ... <sup>16</sup>For God so loved the world, that he gave his only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life. <sup>17</sup>For God did not send his Son into the world to condemn the world, but in order that the world might be saved through him.
4.2 - Discovery Question 1: What does this passage tell you about God?
4.3 - Discovery Question 2: What does this passage tell you about people?
4.4 - Discovery Question 3: What is this passage calling you to do or believe?

You have read a passage, considered what it says about God and people, and named a response. Keep that rhythm close: Read, discover, respond. You can begin with what is clear while continuing to ask questions about what you do not yet understand.
Live What You Discover
Jesus told a story about two builders who heard His teaching. One built on rock, and the other built on sand. The difference became clear when a storm came.

Everyone then who hears these words of mine and does them will be like a wise man who built his house on the rock. And the rain fell, and the floods came, and the winds blew and beat on that house, but it did not fall, because it had been founded on the rock.

The wise builder heard Jesus' words and acted on them. That is why the third Discovery Question matters. A passage might call you to trust God's promise, ask forgiveness, or care for someone. Choose a response that fits what you read. Obedience is a response to God's love, not a way to earn it.
A Tool You Can Share

You do not have to know every answer before you can read with a friend. Open a short passage, listen to what it says, and use the same three questions. If something puzzles you, you can seek help. You are passing on a way to listen to God's Word, not presenting yourself as an expert.
4.5 - How would you explain the Three Discovery Questions to a friend who has never read the Bible?
blocks.data_question: 4.5 - Explaining Discovery Questions to a friend

blocks.text: This Week's Practice

Choose a time to read that fits your life. Use a physical Bible, an app, or an audio Bible if listening helps. As you read this week's chapters of John, pause over a short passage and ask the Three Discovery Questions. Write one sentence about what it calls you to do or believe, then return to that response during the day. If you miss a day, begin again with the next passage.
Lesson 4 Review

God gives you His Word so that you can know Him and follow Jesus. Read, discover, respond. Ask what the passage tells you about God, about people, and what it calls you to do or believe. You can use these questions in your own reading and share them with a friend, while continuing to learn.
In the next lesson, you will see that God never meant for you to do any of this alone.

blocks.heading: Introduction to John 10, 11, and 12
blocks.intro: In John 10-12, Jesus calls Himself the Good Shepherd who lays down His life for His sheep, raises Lazarus from the dead after four days in the tomb, and enters Jerusalem as King. As you read, try using the Three Discovery Questions you learned today: What does this tell me about God? What does it tell me about people? What is it calling me to do or believe?
